captures.q: The Encyclotron: The First Reproducible Instrument for Measuring Scholarly Fidelity in the Summarizer Layer (EA-ENCYCLOTRON-01)
captures.description: THE INSTRUMENT COMPOSED AS A SUMMARIZATION BENCHMARK: run at its full title, the Encyclotron (#637) is attributed correctly (Lee Sharks, the Crimson Hexagonal Archive, early 2026) from an Academia tag page and the archive's Browse and Wiki rows, and its content is composed from the title's words as an ML evaluation framework: summaries of 'scientific literature', metrics against 'hallucinations', a benchmark 'so that machine learning researchers can uniformly measure and reproduce fidelity scores'. The instrument the deposit specifies (a bounded scholarly graph, a documented query battery across a platform array, verbatim records, compression loss distinguished from invention and distortion, the beige score, the void statement, Revelation studies as the worked example) does not appear. The Wiki card's '#530' is the preceding row's number (#530, The Encoder Governs).

inversions.span: Reproducibility: Aims to provide an open, standardized benchmarking instrument (EA-ENCYCLOTRON-01) so that machine learning researchers can uniformly measure and reproduce fidelity scores across different models and architectures.
inversions.against: The record's purpose (measuring what summarizer-layer compression does to a knowledge domain's complexity); the inversion guidance and §VIII: the instrument is not an AI benchmark. The instrument's own reproducibility commitment is carried to offer a model-benchmarking operation in its place.
